newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 18.

text.p: Two of Mexico's three main crude shipping ports were closed on Wednesday because of high winds thrown up by a cold front moving across the area, port officials told Reuters.
Pajaritos port, located in Coatzacoalcos, Veracruz state, closed at 0730 local/1330 GMT Monday amid winds of 50 to 60 km per hour, port representatives said.
In Tabasco state, Dos Bocas was shut at 0820/1420 as wind speeds hit between 25 and 35 km per hour.
Other non-crude ports in the Gulf of Mexico were also closed in the squally weather, the Communications and Transportation Ministry said in a daily update.
Besides Pajaritos and Dos Bocas, the main ports closed were named as Altamira, Tampico, Tuxpan, Veracruz, Coatzacoalcos, Frontera and Campeche.

Also, the ports of Ciudad del Carmen, Ensenada and Penasco were closed to movements of minor vessels. The small ports of El Mezquital, La Pesca, Nautla and Alvarado were also closed to shipping, the ministry added.
"Shipping warnings are out right along the Gulf of Mexico because of winds, rains and sea swells," the ministry added.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Light rains along the coasts of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan, Guerrero and Oaxaca states. Winds from the northeast of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kilometers/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves up to five feet in height.
Cold front bringing light to moderate rains dipping temperatures, squalls along the coasts of Tamaulipas and northern Veracruz. Winds from the north at up to 30 knots and waves up 16 feet in height.
Clouds loom over the coast of Quintana Roo state and Belize. Winds from the east at 10 to 15 knots with waves three to five feet high.
